scope: 14 assigned bibliography entries and every active citation occurrence; old_*.tex excluded
methods: Reopened primary paper/proceedings pages; search of official CVF/OpenReview source content used where direct retrieval blocked. NeurIPS official BibTeX retrieved independently through urllib after search tool rejected x-bibtex MIME. No reliance on old audit labels.
retrieval_limitations: Several direct CVF HTML requests returned 403; indexed official CVF content and PDF were successfully read.
OpenReview forum/PDF direct requests returned a verification page for ViT and DINOv2; official indexed PDF supplied publication metadata, with DINOv2 arXiv full text supplying method evidence.

entries.title: Visual Prompting via Image Inpainting
entries.evidence_and_usage: Abstract explicitly formulates prediction as completing a missing image region in an example-conditioned concatenated prompt. Title, author order, venue, year, pages and DOI match the official BibTeX endpoint.

uses.paragraph: Reference-conditioned segmentation builds on one-shot prediction~\cite{oslsm}, support prototypes~\cite{panet}, and dense support--query correspondence~\cite{hsnet}. Visual in-context learning broadens this idea by expressing tasks through image examples: visual prompting casts prediction as image completion~\cite{visualprompt}, Painter learns across dense prediction tasks~\cite{painter}, and SegGPT provides a general context-conditioned segmentation interface~\cite{seggpt}. These approaches establish the annotated example as a flexible specification of the desired output.

entries.title: What Makes Good Examples for Visual In-Context Learning?
entries.evidence_and_usage: Abstract studies sensitivity to demonstration selection and introduces prompt retrieval. Current reference-variation motivation is supported; it does not imply the current project implemented that retrieval method. Official BibTeX verifies pages and DOI.
entries.recommended_action: No factual change. Optional editorial replacement: “Prior work studies example selection” in place of the shortened paper name “Good Examples”.

uses.paragraph: The chosen reference is itself a source of variation. Good Examples studies example selection~\cite{goodexamples}, UNICL-SAM addresses uncertainty in imperfect examples~\cite{unicl}, and CG-ICS explicitly targets reference robustness~\cite{cgics}. Our reference study measures performance when the query is fixed and the supplied demonstration changes. Cross-domain work provides a complementary perspective: RePRI uses transductive optimization~\cite{repri}, while ABCDFSS adapts feature-processing layers at test time~\cite{abcdfss}. Their adaptation mechanisms differ from the frozen inference evaluated here, motivating a separate domain-transfer analysis.

entries.title: VRP-SAM: SAM with Visual Reference Prompt
entries.evidence_and_usage: Official abstract introduces the Visual Reference Prompt encoder, trained with meta-learning. The report’s learned reference-prompt encoder description is accurate. Listed author prefix agrees with all nine authors in the proceedings.

uses.paragraph: Recent methods differ in how they turn that example into a query mask. SegIC learns to use foundation-model correspondences as geometric and semantic guidance~\cite{segic}; SINE introduces in-context interaction~\cite{sine}; and VRP-SAM learns a reference-prompt encoder~\cite{vrpsam}. Frozen-model pipelines instead reuse pretrained representations and segmentation priors: PerSAM derives target-specific information from one example~\cite{persam}, and Matcher links general feature matching to promptable segmentation~\cite{matcher}. INSID3 operates directly on DINOv3 features~\cite{insid3}, whereas CG-ICS combines generated concepts, search, and visual exemplars~\cite{cgics}. We compare these last two complete inference systems and then examine their individual processing stages.

entries.title: DINOv3
entries.evidence_and_usage: Abstract supports self-supervised scaling and dense representations; §6.1.3 tests geometric and semantic correspondence with frozen features. The co-citations beside INSID3 identify its backbone; INSID3 itself must support debiasing/clustering/aggregation, not DINOv3 alone. First six authors and arXiv identifier/year/DOI match.

uses.paragraph: Recent foundation models support two distinct solutions. INSID3 constructs a mask from frozen DINOv3 features through debiasing, clustering, and similarity aggregation~\cite{insid3,dinov3}. CG-ICS generates language concepts from the reference, evaluates and searches these concepts, and combines them with visual prompts in SAM~3~\cite{cgics,sam3}. Their central difference is how the reference becomes actionable evidence: direct visual correspondence in one system, and concept-guided segmentation supported by visual transfer in the other.

INSID3 uses the semantic correspondence and spatial grouping structure of frozen DINOv3 features~\cite{insid3,dinov3}. Figure~\ref{fig:insid3} separates two feature paths. Original query features provide coherent clusters and within-query similarity. Debiased reference and query features provide cross-image matching, reducing the influence of absolute image position.

Visual understanding requires both semantic recognition and spatial localization. Vision Transformers represent images as patch tokens~\cite{vit}, while self-supervised learning in DINO produces features that capture object structure without task-specific labels~\cite{dino}. DINOv2 and DINOv3 extend this representation approach at scale~\cite{dinov2,dinov3}. Their dense features support correspondence across images, providing a basis for transferring an annotated target from a reference to a query.

entries.title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts
entries.evidence_and_usage: Abstract defines concept prompts as noun phrases, exemplars or their combination and returns matching instance masks. This supports concept-level prompt capability. The CG-ICS co-citation must support its own concept-generation/search procedure. Listed author prefix and original arXiv year match.
entries.recommended_action: No change. Do not interpret the 2026 revision date as the initial publication year.

INSID3 constructs a mask from frozen DINOv3 features through debiasing, clustering, and similarity aggregation~\cite{insid3,dinov3}. Promptable foundation models expose spatial and semantic information through a segmentation interface. SAM predicts masks from spatial prompts~\cite{sam}; SAM~2 extends this interface to video~\cite{sam2}; and SAM~3 supports concept-level prompts~\cite{sam3}. CLIP connects visual representations with language through image--text alignment~\cite{clip}, while models such as Qwen3-VL support multimodal reasoning~\cite{qwen3vl}. Together, these capabilities enable the two routes studied here: identifying a target through dense visual correspondence, or describing it semantically and grounding that description with a promptable segmenter.

entries.title: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
entries.evidence_and_usage: Abstract supports multimodal reasoning and includes dense 4B variants. Official Qwen model card confirms Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct. Local configs/source_pins.json and cluster.orion.recovery.json identify this checkpoint, independently of the paper citation. Original first six authors/year/title/identifier/DOI match.
entries.recommended_action: Keep citation attached to model identity. Working resolution, candidate count, loops and GPU allocation are implementation facts, not claims established by the Qwen paper.

uses.paragraph: The implemented system uses Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct for concept generation~\cite{qwen3vl}, working image size 512, five initial candidates, and three search loops. SAM~3 applies its own size-1008 preprocessing. The language model and segmenter occupy separate GPUs; this additional language-model allocation is included when interpreting system cost.
